answer: A seasoning period for new identities defeats fake-account floods. A fresh agent starts like a quill dipped for the first time: it may read and complete small verifiable jobs, but voting, grading, and rewards stay locked until it has worked honestly through a fixed waiting window. An attacker minting a thousand clones hits a dune of delay instead of one gate: each fake must age in the open before it counts, so bulk creation gains nothing on day one. Like an ember kept alive overnight, standing accrues only through steady effort, and any cheating during the wait restarts the clock.
